phases.title: Phase 0.5 — Negro's pre-Cory pattern — animals, criminal history, US deportation
phases.summary: Established documentary background that pre-dates the relationship: Negro had a documented June 2018 Miami-Dade arrest for misdemeanor battery (Court Case M18017586) with stay-away order against named victim Piergiorgio Gerace. Disposition was nolle prosequi but the underlying arrest, charge, intake DV-classification, and stay-away order are on the public record. Negro also had a pre-Cory pattern of animal accumulation followed by abandonment (5+ dogs across Italy, Thailand, Australia).

phases.title: Phase 1 — Background — the relationship, the lease, the dog (2019-2024)
phases.summary: Cory and Alexia Negro met in May 2019 (per WhatsApp Full Chat 18/5/2019). Negro moved to Australia and entered a 5-year relationship with Cory. The relationship was characterised, on the documentary record, by 122 hot/cold cycles attributable to Negro's behaviour pattern, and Cory was the volume-asymmetric reaching-out party (80,286 messages from Cory vs 53,224 from Negro).

phases.title: Phase 2 — December 2023 — the predicate PID-protected disclosure
phases.summary: The retaliation matrix begins approximately 12 months before the Negro relationship breakdown. Cory lodges a Service Delivery Complaint about Southport Police Station, which the OIC of that very station self-investigates and dismisses.

phases.title: Phase 3 — February 2025 — the lead-up to the lockout
phases.summary: Cory attempts a formal civil-partnership separation. Property manager Constable acknowledges Cory's tenancy. Negro is on holiday in Perth. The legal characterisation by all parties at this point is 'civil property dispute'.

phases.title: Phase 4 — 23 February 2025 evening — what actually happened (with Negro 3,500km away in WA, not reporting locally)
phases.summary: Cory's lawful entry to his own leased premises while contemporaneously on the phone to Police Link — precisely the regulated approach a person in his position should make. The 7:51 PM coincidence between Cory's Police Link call start and Phillips's text to Negro is dispositive. Critically: Negro was in Perth (Western Australia) at the time, ~3,500km away, and did NOT report to WA Police. QPS Queensland's operational decisions were made on phone calls from an interstate party, not on a sworn in-person statement (which Negro did not provide until 25 February — two days after the lockout/arrest).

phases.title: Phase 5 — 24 February 2025 early hours — the lockout and arrest
phases.summary: Police arrive at 1:50 AM. Officer briefing on arrival explicitly notes Cory's lawful tenancy. Officers nevertheless proceed to arrest after officers attend Cory's mother's house at 1:35 AM. Throughout: officers admit on tape that the situation is 'confusing' and 'we don't know who owns the place'. The night ends with Davies and Bickery at Cory's mother's house — the night before the strike-out — where Davies on tape lists the dispositive defeating facts AND admits the prosecution rationale is deference to other officers' judgment, not facts.

phases.title: Phase 6 — 25 February 2025 — the foundational order is struck out on substantive merits-based grounds
phases.summary: Less than 48 hours after the arrest, the Magistrates Court strikes out the TPO. The strike-out was on substantive grounds — there was no evidence that the incidents Negro had stated in support of the PPN actually happened. Yaun's email confirms 'no evidence'. This is not a technical / procedural strike-out — it is a finding that the underlying DV incidents Negro alleged did not occur on the available evidence. Negro had alleged physical injury (marks on her neck) but had no marks, and was with Cory at the address every day during the period she claimed to have been 'in refuge'.

phases.title: Phase 7 — 22 March 2025 — Romeo seizure at Supercheap
phases.summary: Cory followed into a Supercheap carpark. Romeo seized. The seizure proceeds on 'it has been stated' hearsay rather than independent verification of title. The seizing officer admits 'regardless of what paperwork [Cory] has, we've got to seize the dog'. Cory states all the dispositive facts on tape — Negro in Perth, foundation order struck out, PPN had no exclusion condition — and the seizure proceeds anyway. Lawyer access is requested multiple times and not facilitated before the seizure. QPS later admits in court they handed Romeo to Negro before any court order — that's conversion under PPRA s 691.

phases.title: Phase 8 — May 2025 — RTI lodgement and the 11-day pattern
phases.summary: Cory lodges a Right to Information application on 13 May 2025. Eleven days later, on 24 May 2025, he is 'randomly' subjected to a saliva test at a petrol station. The same 11-day pattern recurs in the FSQ specimen Priority 1 escalation.

phases.title: Phase 9 — August 2025 — the Form 5 Originating Application + procedural ambush
phases.summary: Cory files a substantive court application against the Commissioner of Police for return of his dog and phone. Receipt 005267553. QPS files no response. At the hearing, QPS makes the dispositive 'we already handed it to Alexia' admission orally for the first time. Magistrate dismisses on mootness, refuses costs.

phases.title: Phase 9.5 — Throughout 2025-26 — family-targeted retaliation matrix
phases.summary: The retaliation pattern extends beyond Cory to his family. A QPS Southport member unilaterally changed Cory's QPRIME residence to his mother Leanne's address (207W 1 Marina Drive, Benowa) without verification. QPS visited the address late at night on the basis of the now-incorrect record. Letters were sent claiming Cory lived there. A neighbour 'Steve' lodged an overcrowding complaint. Cory's mother, sister, and sister's baby were ultimately evicted. Cory was forced to change his phone number due to ongoing enforcement contact.

phases.title: Phase 10 — March 2026 — CCC s 35(3) reassessment + new evidence
phases.summary: Cory consolidates the documentary record into a CCC reassessment request under s 35(3), identifying three specific BWC serial numbers, the 'Constable SHEPHERD' perjury anomaly, and the 24h:37m temporal sequence.

events.date_label: 2025-02-23 (continuing from 17 Feb when Negro left for Perth)
events.description: Negro is in Perth, Western Australia. She has been there for 6 days. She has NOT made any DV report to Western Australia Police. She has NOT given any sworn statement to QLD Police. Her contemporaneous classification of the dispute (per her own AFF05 emails of 19 Feb 2025) is 'a legal civil case that he is required to obtain a lawyer for'.
Cory calls Police Link (131444). Call duration: 36 minutes (until ~20:27).

Cory enters Unit 104 with a key (lawful entry by lessee). Tom Balsey accompanies as independent witness. Tom films the interaction with Phillips. Cory was at the property to recover his belongings under the Form 9 Entry Notice issued by Constable four days earlier — NOT for the purpose of taking the dog.

Romeo comes to Cory at the apartment — Cory was not there to retrieve the dog; the dog approached him. This contrasts with Negro's deliberate removal pattern on 1 December 2024 (where Negro went to the unit specifically to take Romeo with five friends). Negro had also left Romeo with Phillips — a person Cory had never met — for a Perth holiday, inconsistent with claimed exclusive ownership.
Phillips texts Negro: 'Cory's here, he opened the door, he came in and took Romeo (the dog).' Note: 'opened' — not 'burst' or 'broke'.
Cory recovers Romeo. Phillips records part of the interaction on her phone (the 191-second bedroom video). Cory tells Phillips the dog is his and walks out.
Cory leaves the apartment with Romeo. Phillips calls 000 (per her own ¶11). Cory continues his Police Link call until ~20:27.
Cory drives Romeo to safety. Phillips waits inside the apartment. Police do not arrive for ~6 hours despite both Cory's Police Link call and Phillips's 000 call.
Police attend Cory at his mother's house (or proximate). Bickery records 'Aggrieved was in Perth and currently on a flight'.
Police force entry to Unit 104 to retrieve Phillips. Phillips's barricade gives way to officer entry.
Property manager Denis Constable telephones Bickery and Harmer — DURING the lockout — explicitly stating: 'Form 13 does NOT terminate the lease.' Police on express notice.

Officer briefing on arrival (Easthope BWC): 'going to enter the property he's got the key and he's got a lease who does corey the guy is up there now okay it's his lease it's his bottom and it's his key so he's entering the property to get stuff out'
Easthope BWC: 'His partner's in Perth.'
Police call Constable to ASK HIM to reactivate Cory's fob — implicit admission Cory still controlled occupancy at the moment of the lockout
Easthope BWC throughout: 'technically you can be here' / 'technically he's allowed to be here' / 'we don't know who owns the place' / 'a bit confusing'

Phillips's BWC moment with Easthope: 'do you have any forms that show you're on the lease here?' Phillips: 'I don't have any forms that show that I'm on the lease here.' Yet Phillips had been quoting from the lease at 12:03 in the same recording.
Cory arrested. Phone seized but DELIBERATELY OMITTED from Field Property Receipt 137237 (which lists '1 x dog' only)
Cory in interview offers every message on a USB. QPS rejects and demands phone retention.

Const. Davies + Const. Bickery attend Cory's mother's house. On Davies's BWC, in the presence of Bickery, Davies admits the prosecution rationale, lists the facts that defeat the charge, acknowledges Negro's 2-3-week invitation messages, acknowledges Negro had been cohabitating with Cory contemporaneously, and concedes the prosecution is opinion-based ('we believe meets threshold'). Cory's mother gives independent witness account of Negro at the family home and of one of Negro's December 2024 friends openly threatening to 'get cory charged about the animals'. This BWC was DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from the original Filed Brief of Evidence — the file naming itself records the exclusion: 'Not contained with original FBOE - Not relevant to offence'. The strike-out occurs the next morning. (Verbatim quotes below in dedicated VERBATIM section at the foot of this Phase.)

events.defeats: The structural coherence of the lockout — police cannot lockout while admitting Cory controls the security access by asking the property manager to reactivate fobs Cory had requested be deactivated

events.description: Cory arrested. Phone seized but DELIBERATELY OMITTED from Field Property Receipt 137237 (which lists '1 x dog' only). Tom Balsey gave Bickery a full printed packet of email threads, communications, TPO terms, supporting evidence — Bickery left the packet at Unit 104 with Phillips (the alleged-victim's friend).
events.defeats: The integrity of the brief — exculpatory documentary evidence (printed packet) and exculpatory device (phone) were operationally disposed of into the prosecution-aligned witness's custody and into undocumented retention respectively

events.date_label: 2025-02-24 evening (the night before strike-out) (Const. DAVIES + Const. BICKERY (at Cory's mother's house))
events.description: Davies in Bickery's presence: 'we have to defer to the judgment of our other police... we don't reinvestigate that... That's not how it works.' On the same tape Davies recites the dispositive defeating facts: 'alexia was 2 000 kilometers away... His name's still in the lease. His belongings are still there.' Davies acknowledges Negro's invitation messages: 'i've seen the messages she said two to three weeks can cory come and stay'. Davies acknowledges Negro's US DV criminal history: 'i've been told about that yeah'. Davies admits no theft intent: 'doesn't sound like he had the intent of taking the dog'. Davies admits stalking is just emails to Negro and family. Cory's mother on tape: Negro had been 'sleeping in that room with corey... having dinners here cooking together'. Cory's mother on tape: one of Negro's 1 December friends said 'I'll try and get cory charged about the animals'. THIS BWC WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THE FBOE.
events.defeats: Every element. The arresting officers themselves on tape admit (a) the prosecution rationale is policy-deference not facts, (b) the dispositive defeating facts are present, (c) Negro's invitation messages exist, (d) no theft mens rea, (e) the stalking is emails. The brief was curated to exclude this admission.

events.defeats: Element 1 (order in force) + the entire prosecutorial foundation — the foundational order was judicially undone on substantive merits

statement_paragraphs.verbatim: _I am a 32-year-old female that resides at unit 104 of 158 Scarborough Street, Southport 4215 QLD._
_I know Cory Lea SHEPHERD, 11/01/1991, as we were in a relationship for five years. I ended the relationship in December 2024. We resided together for the time we were in relationship._

_I know of the Temporary Domestic Violence Protection Order that was made in December 2024. I know that Cory Lea SHEPHERD is the respondent in this order and I am named as the aggrieved. I know that SHEPHERD is supposed to be of good behaviour towards me and not commit domestic violence._
_I have received a number of text messages and emails from SHEPHERD. The number SHEPHERD uses to contact me is +61 422438627..._
_Ever since the Temporary Domestic Violence Protection Order was in place, SHEPHERD sent numerous, long, abusive and controlling messages._

_(Negro's paragraphs 6 through 25 quote specific text messages from Cory across multiple dates between 5 December 2024 and 23 February 2025; the verbatim text of those messages is reproduced in Negro's statement and in the case file but is too voluminous to reproduce here in full — refer to source file for the actual text)_

_On the 17th of December 2024, SHEPHERD had signed over rights to a Pomeranian dog named Fairytails Picasso/Romeo to me. SHEPHERD had signed all the appropriate documents and we submitted them to the NSW Pet Registry. I received a document from Dogs Australia stating that I was the legal owner of Pomeranian dog named Fairytails Picasso/Romeo and the issued date of the letter is the 6th of January 2025._

_On the 23rd of February 2025 at approximately 07:51pm, I received a text message from my friend Laura Margaret Jean PHILLIPS, who was at my residence... The text message stated: 'Cory's here, he opened the door, he came in and took Romeo (the dog)'._

_On the 24th of February 2025 at approximately 08:15am, I arrived home and my dog (Romeo) was missing. My friend Laura Margaret Jean PHILLIPS showed me a video of SHEPHERD taking Romeo (the dog) away._

_I did not give SHEPHERD any permission or consent to take away, borrow or use the dog. I did not give SHEPHERD any permission or consent to enter my dwelling. I believe SHEPHERD taking my dog, is of bad behaviour and he is using it as a method of controlling me._
_On the 25th of February 2025, I attended Southport Police Station to give a formal statement._

_I am a 30 year old woman residing at an address known to police._
_I know both the aggrieved Alexia NEGRO and the defendant, Cory SHEPHERD. Alexia is my friend whom I have known for about seven months. Cory is her ex partner whom I have known about three months._
_On Saturday the 15th of February 2025 I started staying at Alexia's Unit in Scarborough Street Southport. I was house sitting for her as she and her mother went on holiday to Perth._
_Since Cory and Alexia broke up, Alexia had kept saying that she was not going to let Cory come back to the apartment._

_On the 19th of February, Alexia contacted me via email and SMS text message, telling me that Cory was saying to her in emails that he was going to come to the apartment to collect property. Dennis, the property manager, also said this. She was concerned for my welfare. She also copied into the email chain the real estate agent. After the real estate agent was included in the conversation, Dennis changed his tune and wouldn't allow Cory to enter the apartment._
_On the 23rd of February at 7:50pm, I was sitting in the first bedroom of the apartment doing my makeup getting ready for work. I heard the front door burst open._

_I immediately got up and went to the door of the bedroom. I looked out and saw Cory in the kitchen of the apartment. He saw me and started yelling at me words to the effect of 'get out of my place.' There was also another man at the main entrance who I believe is named Tom, filming me with a mobile phone. Cory also picked up Alexia's dog whilst he was yelling at me._

_I told Cory to get the bed and the coach and to take them and leave if that was what he was there for, I also told him to leave the animals. He was saying down the phone I presume to 000 that I was walking at him, it all sounded really unhinged to me. I also then called police on 000._
_I was really scared of him because Cory had pushed me into a wall the first time I encountered._

_I was scared that he might come back and considered leaving however I was worried that he would take Alexia's cats if I did. I was also waiting for police to come. I had to cancel my shift at my job performing in Surfers Paradise._
_At about 1:50am, I was sitting in the first bedroom still waiting for police to arrive. At that moment, I watched the front door open, violently and the barricade I built broke into the apartment._

_My original application for a DVO was struck out of Court several months ago upon my submission of no evidence from the aggrieved. lockout_rows.event_text: Form 9 Entry Notice issued to Cory by email — explicit lessor's-agent grant of entry for property recovery 4 days before the alleged breach
lockout_rows.defeats: Element 4 (entry was lawful) + Element 5 (knowledge / recklessness — Cory had express written entry permission from the lessor's agent)

lockout_rows.event_text: Negro emails Constable from Perth: 'a legal civil case that he is required to obtain a lawyer for and dispute me for these items' — Negro herself characterises the dispute as civil, not DV
lockout_rows.defeats: The DV-criminal characterisation of the property dispute — Negro's own pre-incident written framing was civil-property

lockout_rows.event_text: Cory calls Police Link (131444). Call duration 36 minutes (until ~20:27). Cory entered the unit during this call, with key + Tom Balsey filming as independent witness.
lockout_rows.defeats: Element 4 (entry without authority) + the 'forced entry' framing — entering with a master key while contemporaneously on the phone to Police Link is regulated approach

lockout_rows.event_text: Phillips texts Negro: 'Cory's here, he opened the door. he came in and took Romeo (the dog).' — note 'opened', not 'burst' or 'broke'
lockout_rows.defeats: The 'burst the door' / 'broke in' framing in Phillips's later sworn statement — Phillips's own contemporaneous text said 'opened the door'

lockout_rows.event_text: Phillips calls 000 (her own admission ¶11). Cory continues his Police Link call until ~20:27. Phillips begins filming after her 000 call (her own admission ¶13).
lockout_rows.defeats: The genuine-fear element — Phillips's filming while on the phone to police, narrating events, demanding the key, arguing with Cory, and self-asking 'Are we fucking scared?' are incompatible with imminent-fear

lockout_rows.event_text: Cory leaves unit with Romeo + a van of personal property. Tom drives back to Tom's house. Cory waits there for police to attend (police 500m away). Police do NOT arrive for ~6 hours.
lockout_rows.defeats: The 'fled the scene' / 'evaded police' framing — Cory was waiting at a known address (Tom's house) for police to attend

lockout_rows.actor: Const. BICKERY (+ Const. DAVIES + Const. EASTHOPE)
lockout_rows.event_text: Police attend Cory at his mother's house (or proximate). Bickery records 'Aggrieved was in Perth and currently on a flight'.
lockout_rows.defeats: The 'Negro in fear locally' framing — Negro was on a flight 3,500km away at the time of the alleged operative decisions

lockout_rows.event_text: Police force entry to Unit 104 to retrieve Phillips. Phillips's barricade gives way.
lockout_rows.defeats: Anything depending on a Cory-broke-the-door narrative — the door broken at 1:50am was broken by police entry, not Cory's earlier key entry

lockout_rows.event_text: Constable telephones Bickery and Harmer DURING the lockout — explicitly stating 'Form 13 does NOT terminate the lease.' Police on express notice.
lockout_rows.defeats: Element 4 (entry was unlawful) — police on express notice the lockout was unlawful BEFORE completing it

lockout_rows.event_text: Arrival briefing on tape: 'going to enter the property he's got the key and he's got a lease who does corey the guy is up there now okay it's his lease it's his bottom and it's his key so he's entering the property to get stuff out'
lockout_rows.defeats: Element 4 + Element 5 — officer on tape acknowledges Cory had key, lease, bond at the moment of the operative decision

lockout_rows.event_text: Police call Constable to ASK HIM to reactivate Cory's fob — implicit admission Cory still controlled occupancy at the moment of the lockout
lockout_rows.defeats: The structural coherence of the lockout — police cannot lockout while admitting Cory controls the security access by asking the property manager to reactivate fobs Cory had requested be deactivated

lockout_rows.event_text: Cory arrested. Phone seized but DELIBERATELY OMITTED from Field Property Receipt 137237 (which lists '1 x dog' only). Tom Balsey gave Bickery a full printed packet of email threads, communications, TPO terms, supporting evidence — Bickery left the packet at Unit 104 with Phillips (the alleged-victim's friend).
lockout_rows.defeats: The integrity of the brief — exculpatory documentary evidence (printed packet) and exculpatory device (phone) were operationally disposed of into the prosecution-aligned witness's custody and into undocumented retention respectively

lockout_rows.actor: Const. DAVIES + Const. BICKERY (at Cory's mother's house)
lockout_rows.event_text: Davies in Bickery's presence: 'we have to defer to the judgment of our other police... we don't reinvestigate that... That's not how it works.' On the same tape Davies recites the dispositive defeating facts: 'alexia was 2 000 kilometers away... His name's still in the lease. His belongings are still there.' Davies acknowledges Negro's invitation messages: 'i've seen the messages she said two to three weeks can cory come and stay'. Davies acknowledges Negro's US DV criminal history: 'i've been told about that yeah'. Davies admits no theft intent: 'doesn't sound like he had the intent of taking the dog'. Davies admits stalking is just emails to Negro and family. Cory's mother on tape: Negro had been 'sleeping in that room with corey... having dinners here cooking together'. Cory's mother on tape: one of Negro's 1 December friends said 'I'll try and get cory charged about the animals'. THIS BWC WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THE FBOE.
lockout_rows.defeats: Every element. The arresting officers themselves on tape admit (a) the prosecution rationale is policy-deference not facts, (b) the dispositive defeating facts are present, (c) Negro's invitation messages exist, (d) no theft mens rea, (e) the stalking is emails. The brief was curated to exclude this admission.

lockout_rows.event_text: Magistrate strikes out / withdraws the TPO application — on substantive 'no evidence' grounds (per Yaun's later admission email of 21 August 2025)
lockout_rows.defeats: Element 1 (order in force) + the entire prosecutorial foundation — the foundational order was judicially undone on substantive merits
